candidates.angle: the inner motives behind outer austerities
the word anvitah and what it binds them to
candidates.evidence: कामरागबलान्विताः (endowed with desire, attachment, and forceful stubbornness)

candidates.angle: a rejection of self-punishment without guidance
candidates.evidence: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः

angle_en: Anvitah: joined to desire and stubbornness
angle_hi: अन्विताः: काम, राग और बल से सम्बद्ध

en.intro: The Gita looks at the inner state behind outward practices. Listen to the hidden motives Krishna names.
en.notice: The word anvitah means endowed with or joined to. These people are joined to desire, attachment, and stubborn force, which is why their severe austerities do not purify them.
en.next: Krishna then names the ultimate consequence of such misguided self-punishment.
en.meaning: People who perform harsh austerities without scriptural guidance, driven by vanity, ego, desire, attachment, and stubbornness, are not purified by them.

hi.intro: गीता बाहरी कर्मकांडों के पीछे की आंतरिक स्थिति की ओर देखती है। सुनिए, कृष्ण किन छिपे हुए इरादों का नाम लेते हैं।
hi.meaning: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधि से रहित होकर घोर तपस्या करते हैं, जो दम्भ और अहङ्कार से युक्त हैं, जो भोगपदार्थों, आसक्ति और हठ से युक्त हैं, जो शरीर में स्थित पाँच भूतों को तथा अन्तःकरण में स्थित मुझ परमात्मा को भी कृश करनेवाले हैं, उन अज्ञानियों को तू आसुर निश्चयवाले, आसुरी सम्पदावाले समझ।
hi.notice: अन्विताः शब्द का अर्थ है युक्त या सम्बद्ध। ये लोग काम, राग और बल से सम्बद्ध हैं, इसलिए इनकी घोर तपस्या इन्हें शुद्ध नहीं करती।
hi.next: कृष्ण फिर ऐसे भ्रामक आत्मक्लेश का अंतिम परिणाम बताते हैं।

en.intro: The Gita looks at the inner state behind outward practices. Listen to the hidden motives Krishna names.
en.body: People who perform harsh austerities without scriptural guidance, driven by vanity, ego, desire, attachment, and stubbornness, are not purified by them. The word anvitah means endowed with or joined to. These people are joined to desire, attachment, and stubborn force, which is why their severe austerities do not purify them. Krishna then names the ultimate consequence of such misguided self-punishment.

contrast_template: "जो भोगपदार्थों, आसक्ति और हठ से युक्त हैं, जो शरीर में स्थित पाँच भूतों को तथा अन्तःकरण में स्थित मुझ परमात्मा को भी कृश करनेवाले हैं" (The Hindi translation uses the word 'तथा' (and), but the source Sanskrit 'कामरागबलान्विताः' and the English meaning clearly frame this as a list of negative drivers (desire, attachment, stubbornness) that corrupt the austerity. The app's Hindi translation omits the contrastive 'not X but Y' structure entirely, making it sound like these things are simply added to the austerity rather than being the corrupting agents behind it.)
